To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
progesterone and allo are not the cause of PMDD symptoms but are a result of the symptoms.
allo, a progesterone metabolites, is increased in women with PMDD during the lutea phase of ovulatory cycles, and that the severity of the symptoms relates to allo in an inverse U-shaped curve.
progesterone/alo is a GABAA receptor agonist that can induce a paradoxical increase in negative mood at low doses, whereas higher doses are calming.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of GABAA receptor modulation in women’s mood.
the role of allo in relation to mood in the luteal-phase and the role of ISO in PMDD.
the paradoxical effect of allo on mood and its antagonism by ISO.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
allo is anxiogenic in low concentrations and calming in high concentrations, whereas the effects of allo on GABAA receptor function can be antagonized.
allo’s effects are paradoxical and related to allo concentration.
the GABAA modulating steroids have a paradoxical effect on mood and behavior in women.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
allo is a potent modulator of the GABAA receptors and as such can be calming in high concentrations but in low concentrations it can be anxiogenic.
allo’s effects on the brain’s GABAA receptors can be both anxiolytic and negative mood inducing, depending on the dose.
allo and ISO are both GABAA receptor ligands, but allo is a positive allosteric modulator (PAM) whereas ISO is a negative allosteric modulatory (NAM).
The main takeaway from our work is that
GABAA receptor modulation is a double-edged sword.
the GABAA receptors are not just an on/off switch, they can be in different states of modulation, and this modulation can be antagonized.
allo’s effect on GABAA receptors in the brain is not a simple anxiolytic effect.
